text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B engages with the article's actual content, citing that the car 'will steer, accelerate, and brake itself' and that it is 'designed to notify the driver when the road ahead requires human skill,' plus the cameras watching drivers", "quality": "Use of source details", "description": "The essay grounds its argument in specific details from the article rather than making unsupported claims."}, {"evidence": "Essay B raises substantive concerns such as who is to blame in an accident ('You, the car, or the manufacturer?'), road costs funded by taxpayers, and whether a 'safe car' really makes things safer", "quality": "Depth of reasoning", "description": "The essay develops multiple, thoughtful lines of argument that probe real consequences and open questions."}, {"evidence": "Essay B poses rhetorical questions throughout ('Does that sound nice?', 'Is that not scary?', 'who is to blame?') to advance its position", "quality": "Rhetorical engagement", "description": "The essay uses rhetorical questions to draw the reader into the argument and reinforce its points."}, {"evidence": "Essay B has a clear structure moving from an introduction posing a question, through body paragraphs on cost, safety, and control, to a concluding question", "quality": "Organizational coherence", "description": "The essay presents a recognizable introduction, body, and conclusion that build toward its position."}, {"evidence": "Essay A repeats nearly the same sentences in the introduction and conclusion and asserts that cars 'cost a lot of money' and 'add stuff...to just make it look good' without evidence", "quality": "Argumentative development", "description": "Essay B develops and supports its claims while Essay A largely restates a thin, unsupported position."}]}
